raw_quotes.quote: Those four months were exhausting, strained our marriage, and led to arguments.
She'll throw herself on the floor, scream, hit me, bite me — and we're in public. I feel like everyone is judging me as a bad parent.

pain_points: Tantrums in public places leave parents feeling judged and helpless
Physical exhaustion from being kicked, hit, and bitten during tantrums
Marriage strain from disagreements on how to handle tantrums
No clear timeline for when tantrums peak and resolve
Existing advice is generic ('stay calm') without actionable steps
trends.product_angle: The Toddler Tantrum Field Guide — what to do in the moment, how to protect your relationship, and when to worry vs. when to ride it out
trends.ten_page_guide_notes: Cope with physical exhaustion, manage public tantrums, protect your marriage, age-based tantrum timelines, when to seek professional help

raw_quotes.quote: I am having a slight meltdown about the prospect of having to make three meals, every single day, for at least the next decade or two.
Short order cook is my life now. Kid won't eat what we eat. I spend hours per day making separate meals and I'm losing my mind.

pain_points: Making three separate meals (kid food, adult food, family food) every single day
Short order cook dynamic — child refuses family meals
Mental fatigue from daily meal repetition with no end in sight
Guilt when feeding kids processed/picky-friendly foods just to get them to eat
No simple system for batch cooking kid-friendly meals ahead of time
trends.product_angle: The Parent Meal Prep System — batch cooking strategies for kid-friendly meals, a 4-week rotation of simple breakfasts/lunches/dinners, and a 'short order survival kit' for impossible days
trends.ten_page_guide_notes: Batch cooking basics, 4-week meal rotation, pantry staples for quick meals, sibling conflict over food, sanity-saving shortcuts
